title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous and next pages). Pi_0 is the free group of rank 2, identified with the subgroup of SL(2,Z) generated by l_1 = (1 0; 2 1) and l_0^{+-1} = (1 +-2; 0 1). This is the torsion-free index-2 subgroup of Gamma(2), so it has index 12 in SL(2,Z). Its generators lambda_0, lambda_1, lambda_infinity are the three loops of P^1 - {0,1,infinity} and are cyclically permuted by the order-3 automorphism rho. M = Pi_0^ab is free of rank 2. On p.679 Grothendieck introduced the rho-stable submodule M_0 = Z delta + Z rho(delta), with delta = lambda_1 - lambda_0. Since 1 - rho has determinant 3 on M, M_0 has index 3, and it is stable under rho, sigma and tau = -id.

The group N on this page. Let N be the preimage of M_0 in Pi_0. It is a subgroup containing [Pi_0, Pi_0], of index 3 in Pi_0, and normal in the whole group G_0 = GL(2,Z). Modulo N, delta lies in the kernel, so lambda_0, lambda_1 and lambda_infinity all have the same image. With lambda_0 lambda_1 lambda_infinity = 1 this gives the surjection Pi_0 -> Z/3 sending each lambda_i to 1. Geometrically this is the cyclic triple cover y^3 = x(x-1) of the lambda-line, totally ramified at 0, 1 and infinity. That is a genus-1 curve with an automorphism of order 3, i.e. the j = 0 elliptic curve. N is normal of index 3 x 12 = 36 in SL(2,Z), and N does not contain -1.

The question. Grothendieck conjectures that N is a congruence subgroup of level 12, i.e. that N contains Gamma(12). Since |SL(2,Z/12)| = 48 x 24 = 1152, N would then correspond to a normal subgroup of order 1152/36 = 32. That subgroup would be the normal closure of the images of the generators of N: the commutators [sigma_infinity, lambda_infinity] (cf. (7)), delta, and rho(delta). Hence it is the normal closure of the single element delta.

Computation (110). delta = l_1 l_0^{-1} = (1 0; 2 1)(1 2; 0 1) = (1 2; 2 5). He asks whether the normal closure of this element in SL(2,Z/12) really has order 32 (it could be larger) and starts by asking for the order of delta mod 12.

Next page. delta^2 = (5 12; 12 29), which is 5I mod 12, so delta^4 = 1. He then exhibits u x v : SL(2,Z/4) x SL(2,Z/3) -> (group of order 12) x Z/3. The kernel is K4 x Q8, of order 32, and contains delta. Hence the image of N mod 12 is exactly this order-32 group. Its preimage has index 36 and contains N, so it equals N; thus N is congruence of level 12.

Purpose. This belongs to the 'suite' of the Longue Marche: identifying the schemes/group schemes N_{rho,sigma} over Spec Z[1/3] (eq. (107)) with level structures, and checking that a naturally defined rho-invariant cover is modular.
errors: The printed factor (1 +2; 0 1) is l_0^{-1} only if l_0 = (1 -2; 0 1). This is a sign convention; the product (1 2; 2 5) is computed correctly.
The stated index 36 in SL(2,Z) presupposes that Pi_0 is the free index-12 subgroup, not Gamma(2) itself (index 6). This is consistent with the rest but implicit on the page.
The page only formulates the question. Congruence-ness is not proved here; the proof (normal closure of delta of order 32, hence N = preimage) is completed on the next page and is correct in outline.

Implicit step: one must know that the image of N mod 12 is generated by the images of delta and its rho-conjugates (plus commutators). This holds because N is the normal closure in SL(2,Z) of delta together with [Pi_0, Pi_0].

ideas.what: The rho-invariant index-3 subgroup of the free group Pi_0 (kernel of Pi_0 -> Z/3, lambda_i -> 1) is normal in SL(2,Z)/GL(2,Z), of index 36. It corresponds to the cyclic triple cover y^3 = x(x-1), the CM elliptic curve with j = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Normal genus-1 subgroup of the modular group / cyclic quotient of a Fermat-type cover of P^1 - {0,1,infinity}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fricke-Klein); classification of normal genus-1 subgroups by Newman and others; Fermat groups studied by Rohrlich and others
ideas.where_published: Not in La Longue Marche proper as far as I know; this is the unpublished suite

ideas.what: Verifying congruence-ness of a finite-index subgroup by computing the normal closure of a generator's image in SL(2,Z/12) = SL(2,Z/4) x SL(2,Z/3) and comparing indices (36 = 1152/32).
ideas.modern_name: Congruence subgroup test (level 12); Wohlfahrt level, cf. Hsu's congruence test

ideas.what: Use of the order-3 automorphism rho permuting lambda_0, lambda_1, lambda_infinity to define a G_0-stable lattice M_0 = Z delta + Z rho(delta) in Pi_0^ab.
ideas.modern_name: Galois-/automorphism-stable abelian quotients of pi_1 of P^1 - {0,1,infinity} (Z[zeta_3]-module structure on homology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Ihara, Anderson-Ihara on Fermat Jacobians / pro-l towers)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine verification that a natural rho-invariant cyclic cover (the j = 0 elliptic curve over the lambda-line) is a congruence subgroup of level 12. It is interesting as a window into Grothendieck's hands-on modular computations in the unpublished continuation of the Longue Marche. The result itself follows from standard facts and the classification of normal genus-1 subgroups of the modular group, so nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The final paragraph reads: 'La question est donc si ce sous-groupe distingué de SL(2,Z/12Z) est bel et bien d'ordre 32, donc d'indice 36 — son ordre pourrait être plus grand, son indice plus petit. Déjà quel est l'ordre de δ ?' The transcription garbles 'est bel et bien' as 'est bien distingué de bien'.

'il serait donc un sous-groupe [-d'ordre-] {+c'est nécessairement le sous-groupe distingué+} 32': the overwritten word above appears to be 'd'ordre' crossed out, giving 'c'est nécessairement le sous-groupe distingué [d'ordre] 32 de SL(2,Z/12Z), engendré par les éléments images des ...'.
The crossed-out bracket after 'images des' reads '[σ∞, λ∞]' (struck through), with the list then given as the brace system.
